name: Sangoi

spells.name: Invisibility (Self Only)
spells.text:
Illusions bend light around the target, rendering it Invisible. This makes it Undetected to all creatures, though the creatures can attempt to find the target, making it Hidden to them instead. If the target uses a hostile action, the spell ends after that hostile action is completed.

---

Heightened (4th) The spell lasts 1 minute, but it doesn't end if the target uses a hostile action.

spells.name: Speak with Animals (Constant)
spells.text: You can ask questions of, receive answers from, and use the Diplomacy skill with animals. The spell doesn't make them more friendly than normal. Cunning animals are likely to be terse and evasive, while less intelligent ones often make inane comments.

spells.name: Command (Animals Only)
spells.text:
You shout a command that's hard to ignore. You can command the target to approach you, run away (as if it had the Fleeing condition), release what it's holding, drop Prone, or stand in place. It can't Delay or take any reactions until it has obeyed your command. The effects depend on the target's Will save.

---

Success The creature is unaffected.

Failure For the first action on its next turn, the creature must use a single action to do as you command.

Critical Failure The target must use all its actions on its next turn to obey your command.

---

Heightened (5th) You can target up to 10 creatures.

spells.name: Daze
spells.text:
You push into the target's mind and daze it with a mental jolt. The jolt deals 1d6 mental damage, with a basic Will save. If the target critically fails the save, it is also Stunned 1.

---

Heightened (+2) The damage increases by 1d6.

items.name: Sunlight Transparency
items.text: Sunlight causes the sangoi to partially fade from view, growing feeble and translucent. While exposed to direct sunlight, the sangoi is Concealed, Clumsy 1, and Enfeebled 1.

items.name: Blood Rage
items.text:
Trigger The sangoi is reduced below 45 Hit Points by an enemy

---
Effect The sangoi flies into a rage. They gain 20 temporary Hit Points and a +1 status bonus to melee attack rolls but take a –2 penalty to their AC. These effects last for 1 minute or until the sangoi goes a full round without dealing or taking damage, whichever comes first. The sangoi can't end their rage voluntarily.

items.name: Bloodsense
items.text: The sangoi can hear the beating hearts and smell the rushing blood of all living creatures as an imprecise sense within the listed range. They can detect creatures taking persistent bleed damage as a precise sense.

items.name: Curse of Misery
items.text: A creature hit by a sangoi's claws Strike must succeed at a DC 22 Will save save or become cursed for 1 minute. This curse imparts a –1 status penalty to a victim's AC and saving throws against the sangoi who cursed them. In addition, when a cursed victim attempts the flat check to recover from any persistent bleed damage, they must roll twice and take the worse result; this is a misfortune effect.

items.name: Sneak Attack
items.text: The sangoi deals an additional 2d6 precision damage to Off-Guard creatures.

items.name: Vicious Draught
items.text:
Requirements A creature within the sangoi's reach is taking persistent bleed damage

---
Effect The sangoi latches onto the creature's open wound, drinking their blood. They attempt a jaws Strike against the target; if the target is willing, the Strike automatically hits. If the Strike hits, the persistent bleed condition ends, the target is Drained 1, and the sangoi regains Hit Points equal to the target's level, gaining any excess HP as temporary HP. Taking a Vicious Draught from a creature that's already drained doesn't restore any HP to the sangoi but increases the victim's drained value by 1 (to a maximum of Drained 4).

If the sangoi is in a Blood Rage and the jaws Strike reduces the target to 0 HP, the victim must attempt a DC 22 Fortitude save save. On a failure, the sangoi tears out the target's heart and devours it, killing it instantly. This is a death effect.

text: With their nocturnal habits, taste for blood, and proclivity for haunting towns and graveyards in the dead of night, it's unsurprising that sangois are often mistaken for vampires. These smaller fey hunt by following the sounds of their victims' hearts, preferring humanoid victims but settling for animal blood if necessary. They wear roughly cut animal hides to stay warm and are often mistaken for prowling coyotes or wildcats when glimpsed from a window on a cold, misty night.
